newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end off again, mirroring Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end off again, mirroring Dow.

text.p: Brazil shares fell for a third consecutive day as Wall Street's weakness again prompted investors to take profits here, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active stocks closed off 0.92 percent at 9,088 points. Market turnover returned to recent usual levels, totalling 608.3 million reais ($573.8 million).
Bellwether Telebras preferred lost 0.91 percent to 109.40 reais, while its common stock fell 1.43 percent.
0.83 percent to 477 reais, while state mining conglomerate Companhia Vale do Rio Doce lost 0.97 percent to 25.65 reais.

After falling for three days, local stocks are expected to rebound somewhat on Thursday, analysts said. But they noted the market's short-term behaviour continues to hinge on Wall Street as the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee's (FOMC) March 25 meeting approaches.
Anxiety ahead of the FOMC's meeting and a possible hike in U.S. rates has increased market volatility in the last sessions.

Despite encouraging news on the power privatization's front, the Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, closed off 1.28 percent at 2,518 points.

Eletrobras president Firmino Sampaio said earlier at least six-state level power utilities are close to privatization. He said Bahia state power firm Coelba would be privatized by July, while a further five state companies were "virtually ready for sale."
